phase_history.notes: Gain-staged channel strip for modern rap/RnB/drill. Hero feature: Flush Match (automatic input-vs-output loudness matching) so the user never has to guess the output knob after EQ/compression.

Signal flow: Input Trim -> EQ -> Compressor -> Flush Match -> Output. Complexity 3/5. Visage (pure C++) chosen for a FabFilter-style native front end. Mixbus primary use case; M/S + correlation metering; phase-fixing tools deferred to v2.

Pro-Q4-class 24-band dynamic EQ + Flush Match + glue compressor. Complexity 4/5. UNIFIED DYNAMICS ENGINE: one shared detector/gain-computer/ballistics core powers BOTH the glue compressor (broadband instance) and every dynamic EQ band (band-limited instance) - the compressor IS the engine behind dynamic mode. Sound quality is the product: double precision, analog-matched (Orfanidis) biquads, gain-Q interaction, Kaiser-FIR linear phase, 2x/4x oversampling, sample-accurate smoothing, denormal protection. v2 design kept: Pro-Q4 recreation (neon glow nodes/bands/lines, per-band colors), preset browser + A/B, settings modal (UI scaling + accent + refresh), uncapped render loop >=120 Hz, VU<->bar meter toggle, high-quality FFT analyzer. Honest quality goal: reference-class architecture + iterative parity toward FabFilter/Sonnox.

SOLO + DSP QUALITY + ANALYZER pass (80/80 DSP assertions). DSP QUALITY FIX: the EQ was a SERIAL cascade (each band filtered the previous band's already-modified signal -> bands interacted); now PARALLEL (each band filters the DRY signal and contributes a delta, Pro-Q style) — the defining difference for 'Oxford-grade' transparency. BAND SOLO: with parallel topology, delta solo now works — soloing a band plays ONLY that band's contribution (what it adds/removes at its frequency), which is the Pro-Q 'listen to the band' behaviour. COMPRESSOR LOOKAHEAD: 1.5ms lookahead added to the shared DynamicsEngine so the gain ramps BEFORE a transient (no attack grab) — verified (48-sample delay @48k, delayed GR 0 during the window then 7.5dB) and reported to the host via setLatencySamples. ANALYZER: proper FREEZE (hard snapshot — verified it holds while live audio continues, and resumes on unfreeze) + PRE/POST source switch (input vs post-EQ output) + a Freeze/In-Out toolbar on the EQ display. KNOWN BOUNDARY (unchanged, honest): the JUCE/Visage layer is still uncompiled here; first build + visual fine-tune remains the local agent's job (see HANDOFF.md).

framework_selection.rationale: User explicitly wants a FabFilter Pro-Q4-like C++ front end that does not feel web appy. Visage (pure C++, GPU-rendered) delivers native neon-glow knobs/nodes, meters, and a 120 Hz+ render loop with no web stack. Best fit for the interactive EQ display + high-quality analyzer + settings modal.
